 Judgment

Heard Sri.Sanjay S Katageri, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri.M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company.
2. Unsuccessful claimants are in appeal challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.1485/2010 dated 19.09.2011 on the file of the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khanapur, whereby the claim petition against the Insurance Company came to be dismissed.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khanapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of this appeal are as under:
A claim petition came to be filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation in respect of death of a minor child by name Sapna in a road traffic NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 accident that occurred on 29.05.2010 involving a motorcycle bearing temporary Reg.No.KA-22/TR-4824.
4.

The claim petition, on contest, came to be allowed in a sum of Rs.2,25,000/- with interest at 9%
per annum recoverable from the owner of the motorcycle.
5. Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants are in appeal.

6. Sri.Sanjay S Katageri, learned counsel representing the appellants - claimants contended that even though there were two minor children who were sitting on the motorcycle at the time of Deepak Maruti Desai vs Anant S/O Vithoba Savant on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58162693/
2 accident, that itself could not have been a ground for the Tribunal to exonerate the liability of the Insurance Company in toto.

entities.text: Deepak Maruti Desai vs Anant S/O Vithoba Savant
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. He further submits that in the absence of any material evidence placed on record by the Insurance Company that there was a willful violation and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the rider of the motorcycle, the NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 Insurance Company ought not to have been absolved from liability and sought for allowing the appeal.
8.

In support of his argument, he placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mohammed Siddique and Another vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Others reported in (2020) 3 SCC 57.

entities.text: Mohammed Siddique and Another vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Others reported in (2020) 3 SCC 57
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant portions of the said judgment read as under:
"11.
It is seen from the material on record that the accident occurred at about 2.00 a.m. on 5-9-2008.
Therefore, there was no possibility of heavy traffic on the road.

The finding of fact by the Tribunal, as confirmed by the High Court, was that the motorcycle in which the deceased was travelling, was hit by the car from behind and that therefore, it was clear that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the car.
In fact, the High Court confirms in para 4 of the impugned order that the motorcycle was hit by the car from behind.
But it nevertheless holds that 3 persons on a motorcycle could have added to the imbalance.
The relevant portion of para 4 of the order of the High Court reads as follows: (National Insurance Co. Ltd.
Case, SCC OnLine Del) NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 "4.
On careful assessment of the evidence led, this Court finds substance in the plea of the insurance company.

While it is correct that the offending car had no business to strike from behind against the motorcycle moving ahead of it, even if the motorcycle was changing lane to allow another vehicle to overtake, the fact that a motor vehicle meant for only two persons to ride, was carrying, besides the driver, two persons on the pillion would undoubtedly have added to the imbalance."
12. But the above reason, in our view, is flawed.
The fact that the deceased was riding on a motorcycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law.
Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two-wheeled motorcycle, not to carry more than one person on the motorcycle.

Section 194-C,
inserted by Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motorcycle drivers and pillion riders.
Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motorcycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of NC:
2024:KHC-D:814 contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.
It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree, if there had been no violation of the law by the victim.

What could otherwise have Deepak Maruti Desai vs Anant S/O Vithoba Savant on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58162693/
3 resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.

entities.text: Deepak Maruti Desai vs Anant S/O Vithoba Savant
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimised, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked.
It is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three persons riding on a motorcycle.
It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motorcycle.
The fact that the motorcycle was hit by the car from behind, is admitted.

Interestingly, the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the deceased was wearing a helmet and that the deceased was knocked down after the car hit the motorcycle from behind, are all not NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 assailed.

Therefore, the finding of the High Court that 2 persons on the pillion of the motorcycle, could have added to the imbalance, is nothing but presumptuous and is not based either upon pleading or upon the evidence on record.
Nothing was extracted from PW 3 to the effect that 2 persons on the pillion added to the imbalance.

13. Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of the deceased victim contributed either to the accident or to the nature of the injuries sustained, the victim could not have been held guilty of contributory negligence.

Hence, the reduction of 10%
towards contributory negligence, is clearly unjustified and the same has to be set aside."

9. Per contra, Sri.M.Y.Katagi, learned counsel representing the Insurance Company contended that in the case on hand, violation of provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act is at the inception of the incident itself.

Therefore, the principles of law enunciated in the decision referred to in Mohammed Siddique supra is not applicable to the case on hand and the Tribunal has rightly NC:
2024:KHC-D:814 exonerated the Insurance Company and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
10. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

11. On such perusal of the material on record, it is crystal clear that in the complaint itself there is a specific averment that the deceased Sapna had been to marriage at Hattargunji village, Khanapur taluk.
12. The first respondent who is the owner of the motorcycle requested the petitioner that he will take the deceased child on motorcycle and drop her in the house of the claimants.
When the motorcycle reached near Kamataga village, on account of rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle, he lost control over the motorcycle and accident has occurred.

Charge sheet came to be filed against the rider of the motorcycle.
13.
These aspects are not in dispute.

Taking note of the fact that as on the date of the accident, along with the NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 deceased, one more minor child and another major person were also carried on the motorcycle by the rider of the motorcycle, as is rightly contended by the Insurance Company, there was a willful violation of the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act by the rider of the motorcycle at the inception itself.

4 14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Mohammed Siddique supra, the Hon'ble Apex Court has specifically held in paragraph No.13 that it is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three persons riding on a motorcycle.
15. It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motorcycle.

16. In the case on hand, not only Insurance Company has attributed the entire negligent on the part of the rider but the claimants themselves have attributed such negligence on the rider in their claim petition itself.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 17. Therefore, the principles of law enunciated in Mohammed Siddique supra would not be applicable to the case on hand.

18. In other words, if it is a case of three persons being travelling on the motorcycle without there being any negligence attributable to the rider of the motorcycle resulting in injury or death of one of the persons, who have travelled on the motorcycle and the negligence is on the rider/driver of the of another vehicle involved in the accident, then Insurance Company may be held liable.
19. But in the case on hand, it is rider of the motorcycle who is alone responsible for the negligent riding of the motorcycle.
20. Further, having carried two minor children and one major person on the motorcycle, the rider of the motorcycle should have taken utmost care to ride the same so as to reach them safely.
In the case on hand, no - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:814 such conduct has been forthcoming on record insofar as rider of the motorcycle.
21. Under such circumstances, the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation cannot be interfered with by this Court in this appeal.

22. In view of the foregoing discussions, following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Appeal is meritless and hereby dismissed.
 (ii) No order as to costs.
